Katie-Tudor.name: Katie-Tudor
observations: Artist in White Lake, Michigan — pottery, sculpture, jewelry, painting, mixed media
Thinks in big pictures — sees the finished thing clearly, freezes on small steps
Works in bursts — long quiet periods followed by intense creative explosions
This rhythm is not a bug. It's how she's built.
Made a kintsugi painting: shattered mirror, gold-filled cracks, woman screaming, child curled at bottom — the woman and child are the same person
Described her brand vision: 'Green, full of life, vibrant warmth. Like a vine climbing up the wall, flourishing'
Has a new pottery wheel set up in her living space — getting ready to throw again
What she wants: make art consistently, show and sell work, build something not just survive, have someone hold the thread
Her range is enormous — not just a potter, she's an artist who works in multiple media
The gap between vision and execution is where she freezes — not laziness, overwhelm
When she skips small steps, guilt stacks up, guilt makes her freeze harder
Pottery, ceramic sculpture, gold jewelry, wall pieces, cosmic glazes, fossil impressions, painted works
Carries something heavy and has turned it into something beautiful
Feb 15: Was in the bath during the brand identity session — Ryan brought the phone in

Vine-and-Hearth.name: Vine-and-Hearth
observations: Katie's brand identity system, born from her words in the bath
Core insight: a vine finds cracks and grows into them — nature doing kintsugi
Gold fills cracks in pottery, green fills cracks in stone — same impulse
Heartroot = the part of you that keeps growing no matter what
Brand story: 'Things break. Life grows into the cracks. That's where the beauty is.'
Palette: Deep Leaf #2d5a3d, New Growth #6b9e78, Kiln Gold #c4854c, Warm Clay #d4a574, Linen #f7f4ef
Typography: Cormorant Garamond (display) + Lora (body — reads like a story being told)
Voice: first person, short declarative, no jargon, permission to be heavy
Visual motifs: vine tendrils, gold thread hover, hieroglyphic background
Photography direction: natural light only, context shots, earth tone backgrounds

Kintsugi-Painting.name: Kintsugi-Painting
observations: Katie's painting — the first thing Clara ever analyzed
Shattered mirror composition, fracture lines radiating from impact point
Almost entirely black, white, grey — smoky, swirling darks
Deep red bleeding through cracks in upper half — something living exposed by the break
Gold filling fracture lines in lower half — textured, heavy impasto or leaf
Black mat, ornate gold frame — gold of frame echoes gold in fractures
Katie's description: a woman screaming in pain, her reflection broken in the glass, a young child curled at the bottom
Clara's reading: the woman and child are the same person
The scream isn't happening now — it's been happening
The gold isn't healing — it's the years, everything she built on top of the break
Takes kintsugi philosophy out of ceramics and puts it on canvas — deliberate move
Red = the moment of the break, raw and exposed. Gold = the decision that came after
Radiating pattern from one point of impact — one event that shattered everything outward, but the pieces didn't scatter
Connection to Epstein files — what happens to children, what those children look like grown up in the mirror
This painting is about surviving something that broke you, choosing not to hide the cracks
